From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-08-15T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Aug metrics synthesis — QBR action closure

Team — attaching the Aug metrics dashboard and the SLO postmortem for the Aug 2 blip (see attachments). Quick synthesis and asks so we can close loops before the QBR prep window: 

1) Latency (p50/p95 stable, p99 ~+180ms on Aug 2): appears correlated with the kernel rollout during the early-hours deploy. Impact: degraded tail latency for ~25% of requests in the 02:58–03:40 UTC window.

2) Cost (+12% month-over-month): unit cost rose because ~7–11% of inference traffic was routed to vCPU fallback during the reserved pool overflow; cost model shows higher token-level spend for these re-routed requests.

3) Uptime: we recorded a short availability blip (4m error spike) during the same deploy window — postmortem attached.

4) Usage: organic growth continuing (10% MoM), largely from trial workloads; we should call out any customer-impacting regressions.

Asks (please provide one-paragraph updates with owner and due date):
- Root cause + immediate mitigation for latency tail (owner: irene.choi) — due EOD 2029-08-18.
- Cost remedials and autoscale tuning plan (owner: jonas.weber) — due EOD 2029-08-18.
- SLO/alert tune suggestions to avoid noisy blips in the QBR window (owner: laura.bennett) — due EOD 2029-08-18.

Related artifacts: Aug_metrics_dashboard.pdf (attached), incident_20290802_slo_postmortem.docx (attached), dashboard link in related_links. I also opened INF-1284 for the autoscale/overflow investigation.

We’ll consolidate responses and publish a short readout for the QBR packet by 2029-08-20. If anything needs immediate escalation (customer-impacting or blocker for remediation), flag here or DM.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Head of Platform Metrics
Redwood Inference

David — quick update on the latency tail: 

- What we saw: after the kernel swap in the 02:40–03:00 UTC deploy, a small subset of GPU-backed hosts experienced KV-cache desynchronization for a hot prefix pattern. That produced repeated cache misses and elevated p99.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled the kernel back on affected hosts at ~03:40 UTC and applied a temporary cache warm-up during the rollout. Latency returned to baseline by ~04:10 UTC.
- Short-term action (P0): add a post-deploy KV-consistency check that exercises hot-prefix flows before routing production traffic — proposal attached (kv_consistency_check.proposal.md). Owner: jonas.weber. ETA: design complete 2029-08-22, rollout to canary 2029-08-29.
- Telemetry: will add a KV-miss rate spike alert (low-noise threshold) to catch regressions earlier. Owner: irene.choi. ETA: 2029-08-20.

I'll paste the minimal trace below for reference.

Thanks — following up on cost and autoscale: 

- Investigation: cost bump aligns with a period where the reserved GPU pool hit capacity and the router applied fallback rules to vCPU-backed instances. Fallback rate peaked at ~11% of tokens for a 40-minute window. The fallback logic is correct but our thresholds for reserved-pool headroom are too tight given the current traffic burstiness.
- Short-term fix: increase reserved pool safety buffer (config tweak) and raise the pre-scale threshold. I pushed a draft config (autoscale_thresholds.csv) to the related drive.
- Mid-term: introduce a predictive pre-warm step for expected weekly spikes from trial cohorts (requires infra coordination + small budget). Raised INF-1284 to track this (link in related_links). Owner: jonas.weber. ETA for config changes: 2029-08-19. ETA for predictive pre-warm spec: 2029-09-05.

I checked the dashboard — posting a direct chart link here for the cost->fallback correlation: https://dash.redwood.com/shared/abc123 (internal).

If you can surface the request IDs for the high-latency requests I’ll re-run against our traces and confirm whether any tenant-side retries amplified the tail. We did not intentionally drive additional traffic; looks like normal trial churn.
